data.content_ref: inline:{"analogy":null,"claim":"The panel of non-experts is more reliable not because of the checklist's content, but because the act of collective verification creates a 'social error-correction loop' that suppresses the individual cognitive biases (like confirmation bias) that often plague a single expert's intuition.","counterconditions":[{"case":"The panel exhibits high groupthink or deference to a perceived leader.","checker_spec":null,"eval":"observation"},{"case":"The task requires a synthesis of information that cannot be decomposed into checklist items.","checker_spec":null,"eval":"observation"},{"case":"The training of non-experts creates a shared cognitive bias that mirrors the expert's blind spots.","checker_spec":null,"eval":"observation"}],"definitions":[],"derivation":[],"formalization_refs":[],"mechanism":"The causal mechanism is 'Inter-rater Friction': when multiple non-experts must agree on a checklist item, the necessity of justifying a 'Pass' to peers forces a transition from System 1 (intuitive) to System 2 (analytical) processing. This social pressure to provide evidence for each tick reduces the 'blind ticking' seen in individuals and creates a redundancy filter that catches 'expert blind spots'\u2014errors an expert makes because they are too familiar with the task to see the obvious flaw.","premises":[],"schema":"deepreason-reasoning-envelope-v1","scope":{"covers":[],"excludes":[]},"simulation_refs":[],"uncertainties":[]}
